- If sentiment history is uniformly 0.00, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon and underestimates sharp spikes; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for spikes >80.
- If model shows gradual upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day) and true outcome has sharp upward move, reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for the first 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after spike (e.g., 85→80→78), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment history includes 1.00 (positive sentiment), model tends to overreact; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 3–7 days after sentiment spike.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising but true outcome shows strong upward movement, consider 3–5 day lag; shift forecast up by 1–2% for the first 3 days of the true spike.
- For 30-day horizon, if model starts at 78.5–79.5 and true outcome exceeds 85, reduce forecast by 2–4% for the first 5 days, then adjust to match true trend.
